messages:
maya: Heads-up — bringing up raven-embed-6b (int8) in staging. Quick smoke shows a weird drop on short queries (<= 8 tokens).

maya: Baseline (fp16) recall@10 on shortq: 0.87, raven-int8: 0.72. Full eval running but wanted to surface early. :thinking_face:

owen: Oof. Can you paste the eval command you ran?

maya: ran the standard infra script locally:

```
python infra/run_eval.py --model raven-embed-6b --quant int8 --dataset shortq --metric recall@10 --batch 64 --topk 10
```

maya: And the quick output snippet:

```
Dataset: shortq (5k queries)
Baseline fp16 recall@10 = 0.873
raven-embed-6b int8 recall@10 = 0.721
Avg latency/token: fp16 1.9ms -> int8 1.1ms
```

zara: Interesting latency win but quality hit. Any difference in normalization/whitening step?

maya: Same preprocessing pipeline AFAICT. I re-ran with whiten disabled, still ~0.72.

sam: Did you check per-language or per-length buckets? maybe int8 collapses short context semantics.

maya: Yep — bucketed by query length: drop concentrated on 1-4 token queries. Longer queries unaffected.

owen: Could be quantization sensitivity on the embedding head. Do we have per-layer activation ranges to inspect?

maya: Saved activation stats during a short run. Attaching small excerpt:

```
Layer: embed_proj max 6.2 min -5.8 mean 0.02 std 0.91
Layer: mlp_1 max 12.4 min -11.1 mean 0.01 std 1.6
Layer: final_norm max 3.7 min -3.4 mean 0.0 std 0.42
```

maya: Notably embed_proj has heavy tails from rare tokens — might be getting clipped by symmetric quant.

zara: Try symmetric vs asymmetric quant and per-channel vs per-tensor. Also test dynamic range clipping at 99.9 percentile instead of max.

sam: Agreed. Also run a contrastive probe: take top-1 vs top-10 neighbor distances for short queries — check margin shrinkage.

maya: Will run 3 quick variants today:
- int8 symmetric per-tensor (current)
- int8 symmetric per-channel
- int8 asymmetric per-channel with 99.9pct clip

maya: Quick note: running per-channel slows runtime roughly 5-8% on our CPU quant path, but still faster than fp16 on GPU for our bench.

eval-bot: queued evals: 4987654322, 4987654323, 4987654324 (raven-int8 variants). Estimated finish 2h.

owen: Also ping infra to regenerate the KV-cache test dataset — maybe short queries rely on positional idiosyncrasy.

zara: For diagnostics, can you run a paired A/B recall on the holdout set with a small sample of labeled paraphrases? want to confirm semantic collapse vs retrieval boundary shift.

maya: Good call. I'll run pairwise paraphrase recall@1 on 1k pairs. If recall@1 drops similarly, it's semantic. If only recall@10 changes, could be distance scaling.

sam: If scale shift, try applying a post-hoc rescaling (learned temperature) on int8 embeddings and re-evaluate recall@k. Sometimes simple affine scaling recovers a lot.

maya: Notes for action:
1) Run quant variants (symmetric/asymmetric, per-channel) — started.
2) Run paraphrase pairwise recall@1 (1k sample).
3) Compute neighbor-distance distributions (top1/top10) and margin histograms for short vs long queries.
4) Try simple rescaling calibrator on int8 embeddings.

owen: If per-channel helps, we can add it to the int8 profile for raven in staging. If not, we may need to ship raven as int16 or keep fp16 for short-query-heavy customers.

maya: Will post results here when eval-bot finishes. Thanks for quick eyes. :pray:

eval-bot: eval 4987654322 complete — raven-int8-perchannel (symmetric): recall@10 = 0.805 on shortq. Details uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-evals/raven/4987654322/results.json

maya: Nice — per-channel recovered most of the gap. Can someone sanity-check that the per-channel artifacts don't break other workloads?

zara: I'll run the multilang and longtail holdouts overnight. If those look stable, we can set per-channel symmetric as default for raven-int8.

sam: Add a note to the rollout checklist: "validate short-query recall and run margin histogram".

maya: Will update the onboarding doc and add quant profile. Closing provisional triage, will reopen if overnight tests fail. :white_check_mark:
